text: Patient presents with acute chest pain radiating to the left arm. No evidence of myocardial infarction on ECG. History of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Currently taking metformin and lisinopril.
Denies fever, cough, and dyspnea but complains of persistent headache and nausea.
Pneumonia was ruled out by chest imaging. Consider ruling out pulmonary embolism given the clinical presentation. Started aspirin and warfarin for prophylaxis.
Patient with no change in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease symptoms. No nausea or vomiting reported. Previously diagnosed with asthma. Taking albuterol and prednisone.

The patient has a h/o congestive heart failure and is suspected of having deep vein thrombosis. Edema noted in bilateral lower extremities. Denies chest pain or dyspnea but reports diarrhea. Atorvastatin and amlodipine continued.
Pt admitted with myocardial infraction and subsequent cardiogenic shock. No evidence of pneumona on chest X-ray. Started on insulin drip and omeprazole for stress ulcer prophylaxis.
Patient without fever or headache. Not currently experiencing nausea. Previous diagnosis of type 2 diabetes mellitus, now well controlled. Possible pulmonary embolism, CT angiography ordered.
